items.note: N0 states (X_a,Y_a) to (-Y_a,X_a) with every scratch wire restored, and N0.1-N0.4 follow the proof: the net change (JV+RG)x is independent of the scratch values, the bit and complex coefficient checks, and the three-stage chain. The method line wrongly calls all three stages forward invocations (stage 2 is the inverse schedule), but N0.4 corrects this. h=100 and the wire counts are not given.

Same invariant argument as the paper: the logical input is D_in^{-1}f, edges change D_u to D_v, and a common frame commutes with a pointwise linear gate. This gives D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} and the per-route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}.

Every claim is stated correctly: the pairings, interstage matching, side-wire nesting, the central 3->4 loss h, L=Ich, Wm-2N+2L, and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539. But the gate-label table (eq:motif-labels) and the per-edge residual table are only named ('read ... from a table'). So nothing shows why the central return A(x)F -> B(x)F is the only decrease or why it loses h. The F_2 orthonormal-basis argument (L0.5) is restated, not derived.

The steps follow the paper. B0 assigns projections P_U to gates and sinks and -P_{U_a} to X_a sources. B0.1 shows rank equals dimension change, B0.2 identifies the N exceptional source edges 2P_{U_a}, B0.3 gives the deficit N-2L_b>0, and B0.4 the endpoint identity I_m. K0.2 turns that identity into the shear H<-H+D on every role.

P0.1-P0.8 follow the proof: weight additivity mod 4, odd weights, the kernel aI+bX_v, the count s_c, and the X_a->Y_a pair with C^{-1} on 27 coordinates corrected by Z_{a,k} and i^{27k}. The headline P0 says the endpoint operator is C^{(x)m} on every role without saying this holds only after the diagonal corrections and the undoing of the signed exchange.

Both deficits are given: N-2L_b>0 and 2N-2L_c>0, from L/N=100/539 and 101/539 < 1/2. B0.5 reproduces the exponent argument: deficits > 20*2^{-50}, m<2^20, m^{1-2^{-50}} > m(1-20*2^{-50}) > m(1-eta), hence s/W < m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}. The exact eta values are not displayed; R0's justification of s<Wm is loose (see errors).

S1.1 lists the elementary O(V) operations correctly. In its claim, S1.2 drops the condition that the offset be preparable in b^{O(1)} time; only the quote carries it. It also puts multiplication by a rational unit under 'one split and merge', whereas the paper uses c increasing pieces and a block-reversal for negation. Neither proof is reconstructed.

The pivot elimination (topmost row, rightmost entry, lower-triangular operations on active indices) is the paper's. So are the prime choice, linear-time triangular transforms, the conjugation order, and the three-update realisation of each one of Pi with one interchange, which totals exactly a interchanges.

The derivation matches the paper. It covers the cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, Phi_{A_e} on edges via matrix-shear, the frame identity giving H<-H+D on every row, and the three-update swap. It also covers s calls, F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), the two geometric-sum cases, and the fixed-tape parking schedule. K0's hypothesis gives only the total rank s<Wm; it omits the endpoint condition M_out(rho(w)) - M_in(w) = I_m of eq:finite-shear-contract, which comes only through B0.

Follows the proof: rho high digits as the row field, padding to R'=W^k ceil(R/W^k)<2R, base-m pieces handled by power-width calls, the geometric sum O(Ve^tau), padding binary ranges to [q^e], and the one-bit adjustment for unequal widths.

Conjugation by P_M with the residual basis as the first columns. Each inverse child comes from one forward call via (C^{-1})^{(x)f} = (-i)^f Z C Z. M is at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, there are exactly s_c children on f=e/m axes, and H_0^{(x)D} = b^D S_D C^{(x)D} S_D. All as in the paper.

Covers the eight conditional additions with the result (u+c(1-2(u mod 2)), w), each line as one whole-chunk cyclic shift, the guard interval [10, 2^{K-1}-11], and delta_bad by the union bound. Also T_0 S_0^{-1} permuting B, radix-sort repair, the cost terms, and the application to row additions. The separate final XOR at the top position j_{f-1} is not mentioned; this is a small omission.

Follows the paper's analysis. The leaf cost is O(Ve) and the node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)). The first q_0 chunks become the row index, children have volume V/W, and F(e) <= (s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1). The internal geometric sum, the leaf bound e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)} and the base-m split give O(d^{lambda'}).

Statement: O(Vd^{lambda'}) with one final truncation and error < sqrt2 2^{-p} (B0x.1). The guard-width bound is derived as in the paper: A(e) <= sA(e/m)+E, B^{k+1} <= B^2 d^nu, total depth <= C_0 d^{C_1}, depth j gives 2^{-(p+j)} grid and modulus 2^j, and epsilon C_1<1 gives Delta=o(p). The uniform check of the packed-lemma regime over the d,r bands is only implicit.

Character cancellation by index shift with y^{rj_0}=-1. Decimation in frequency puts the output in bit-reversed slots, the reverse traversal realises F^+B^{-1}, and the grouped round with J_E follows. Prefix-slot moves cost O(TpdK), at most Dq-1 chunk exchanges cost O(Tp pK^{tau-1}), and rounds cost O(Tp ell d^{lambda'}). Truncation commutes with J_E, and the output order is L(Bj).

Same signed Kronecker route: B_0=2^{4p}, the separation |h_j| <= r2^{2p} < B_0/2, two's-complement packing with carries in {-1,0}, centered extraction with carries in {0,1}, negacyclic reduction, and truncation by shifting p+ell bits.
Normalization identity, P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v), the error chain 2delta -> 2delta+eta -> 3delta+eta -> M(3delta+eta) = sqrt2 M(3ell+1)2^{-p}, and the cost from M=T/r products, all as in the paper.

Follows the proof. ||N-I|| < 2^{-alpha^2 theta} < 1/2 makes N invertible. The normalisations S', J', D' with A=S' and B_0=D'J'C give the product 2^{-2alpha^2}. The cited error and time table and the ordered selection C are reproduced. The permutations P_t, P_s are kept unsorted, and tensoring gives gamma=2d alpha^2 with linewise error dp^2 and axis exposure O(d^2) swaps.

The chirp has period t_i, and the coefficient comparison against Q's frequency (-s_i j_i) gives the chirp identity. For the cancellation: F^+R_c = R_c^{-1}F^+ gives R F^+ R = F^+, permutations commute with pointwise products, and the convolution rule gives (u*v)/S^2. Conjugation gives the + version.

The parameter values, sizes, and the prime-interval argument (Q1.1-Q1.5: count > d, disjoint intervals, S/T > 1/2, alpha^4 theta_i > p, n^{o(1)} search) are faithful. Not shown: the layer conditions tau(1+c/beta) < lambda and sigma+beta(1-sigma) < lambda' (only some exponent inequalities are listed in PB.1), the gamma <= b/4 bound, and the no-wraparound check 2q-2 < T/2 < S, which M0 only asserts.

Isomorphism via the order-S image of x, the triangular digit formula, the padding scan, and updates in order i=d..1 as prefix-controlled cyclic shifts on valid intervals. Also the explicit inverse and the O(d^2) axis reversal giving O(Tp d^2(1+ell^tau)), all as in the paper.

Well-definedness (zeta y)^r=1, the diagonal isometric isomorphism, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h = zeta^j, M_C = D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g) = f*g/T, and the computed version with twist arrays of error < 2*2^{-p}.

The source transform is A-tilde, the chirp transform, B_0-tilde, then the 2^gamma scale, with exact counterpart RF_s and conjugate F^+. Input digits are scaled by 2^{-b-2}. The six steps match the paper, and M7 explains the two scales by S.

Error chain E_ring < 5TL -> 6TL -> 8TL -> E_s = 9*2^gamma TL -> E_w < 28*2^gamma T^2 L. The final bound 448b 2^{-b+gamma} <= 448b 2^{-3b/4} < 1/2 uses S <= T < 2^b, L < b and gamma <= b/4. Then come rounding, the carry recurrence, and the 2n-bit output, all as in the paper.

Normalized costs as powers of p, the margins g_1..g_7 with min g_2 = 2^{-181} = 2kappa, and the per-row justifications. Setup and exceptional-stream sorting are o(V), log factors are <= p^kappa, and the schoolbook cutoff is used. All match the paper.
S0 says the bound disproves the n log n conjecture in this model, but nothing explains the eventual-lower-bound formulation or why a liminf (here a limit) of zero refutes it.

errors.says: Method: build the exchange from three stages, 'each a forward invocation y_S <- y_S + x_S'.
errors.paper: Stage 2 is the inverse forward schedule from Y to X, which effects X <- X - Y. Only stages 1 and 3 are forward invocations from X to Y. N0.4 states this correctly.

errors.says: The sum over all edges of the label-dimension changes equals Wm-2N+2L, and since L<N/2 this total is strictly below Wm.
errors.paper: The signed sum is Wm-2N; Wm-2N+2L is the sum of absolute changes. For Wm-2N+2L < Wm, L<N is enough. L<N/2 is needed because the bit interface adds N extra source ranks.

errors.says: Updating y by a control-dependent offset, or multiplying it by a fixed rational unit, costs O(V) because the update is a cyclic shift of blocks done by one split and merge.
errors.paper: The O(V) bound needs the offset to be preparable in b^{O(1)} time. Multiplication by a unit c uses a split into c increasing pieces with residue-counter merging, and negation reverses blocks via a stack; neither is a single cyclic shift.

errors.says: Each edge change is a product of kernels aI+bX_v, ..., and the endpoint operator is C^{(x)m} on every role.
errors.paper: On the X_a -> Y_a pair the telescoped operator is C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a) and C elsewhere. C^{(x)m} on every role holds only after the source and sink diagonal corrections and after undoing the signed bank exchange. P0.6-P0.8 supply this.

errors.says: Assume a fixed restoring circuit with W wires and label dimension m whose edge matrices have total rank s<Wm, ... then the chunks can be interchanged in O(Ve^tau).
errors.paper: The contract eq:finite-shear-contract also requires M_out(rho(w)) - M_in(w) = I_m for every role. Without it the frames do not yield the same shear H <- H+D on every row. B0 and K0.2 supply it.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound. Bit network -> frames -> labels -> rank budget -> shear interface -> matrix shear -> power-width recurrence -> arbitrary-width interchange. Complex phase network -> phase-frame recursion -> packed bit additions -> layer recurrence and guard widths -> simultaneous layer. Then synthetic transforms and layout -> ring convolution -> resampling, chirp and permutation cancellation -> primes and CRT -> source transform and algorithm -> exact recovery -> parameter balance with min margin 2kappa. It thins out in three places. The label construction names but does not give the gate-label and residual tables or the F_2 orthonormal-basis argument. The interchange hypothesis drops the endpoint identity, which appears only in the child B0. The parameter conditions and no-wraparound check are only partly shown. h=100 and N=binom(h,3)^3 are never stated.

steps.note: The fixed linear network on X_a,Y_a and scratch wires sending (X_a,Y_a) to (-Y_a,X_a) with every scratch wire restored is given, along with its three-stage mechanism and the triple-indexed coefficient checks; m=h^3 appears in L0. The plan never states h=100 or N=binom(h,3)^3, so the reconstruction is thin on parameters.
A common invertible frame per gate commutes with the pointwise gate. The network implements D_out S D_in^{-1}, and each edge only changes frame by D_v D_u^{-1}.
Labels are nondegenerate subspaces of F^{(x)3} of dimension m=h^3, nested along every edge. The only decreasing edges are the central wires from time 3 to 4, each losing h.
P_V - P_U has rank dim V - dim U for nested U in V. The N source edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one are the exceptions.
Signed total Wm-2N, absolute total Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich, and s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b are all stated.
L/N=100/539 and 101/539, both below 1/2, giving the deficit N-2L_b>0 and s<Wm. The complex deficit 2N-2L_c>0 is also stated.
M_sink(rho(w)) - M_source(w) = I_m on every role, with P_{U_a^perp} - (-P_{U_a}) = I_m for X_a. Through frames Phi_M this gives H <- H+D on every row, including scratch rows.
A=E_1 Pi E_2 with lower-triangular factors. The shear costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V), so a node makes s recursive calls in all.
Children have volume V/W, and F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1). s/W < m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}, from deficits > 20*2^{-50} and m<2^20 (hence log m<20). The two geometric-sum cases give F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the whole chain of the central saving. It covers the fixed bank-exchange network, frames, nested labels with the single decreasing central edge, rank equal to dimension change with the N source exceptions, the budget Wm-2N+2L and s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b, the strict saving from L/N = 100/539 < 1/2, the endpoint identity giving the shear, edges as rank-many recursive interchanges, and the recurrence with tau = 1-2^{-50}. The only thinness is that h=100 and N=binom(h,3)^3 are never stated.
